title: EDiR Practice Set 4 · breast, cardiac and head & neck imaging
subtitle: Radform original question bank · English · used for adaptive practice sessions
disclaimer: Simulacro original de Radform basado en la estructura publicada del EDiR. No contiene preguntas oficiales ni bancos de pago.

questions.question: Which mammographic findings are suspicious? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Spiculation, suspicious calcifications and new distortion warrant diagnostic evaluation.

questions.question: Subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement in a coronary distribution on cardiac MRI suggests:
questions.explanation: Ischaemic injury follows coronary territories and begins in the subendocardium.

questions.question: MRI is particularly useful in head and neck cancer for assessing:
questions.explanation: High soft-tissue contrast makes MRI valuable for skull-base and perineural disease.

questions.question: Which findings support cervical carotid artery dissection? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Mural haematoma, tapered narrowing and pseudoaneurysm are recognised features.

questions.question: The classic differential diagnosis of an anterior mediastinal mass includes which entities? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: The traditional anterior mediastinal differential includes the “4 Ts”.

questions.question: An oval, circumscribed breast mass that is parallel to the skin on ultrasound:
options: May have probably benign morphology depending on context
questions.explanation: Oval shape, circumscribed margin and parallel orientation can be benign features but must be integrated with the full BI-RADS assessment.

questions.question: Imaging findings that may support constrictive pericarditis include:
options: Pericardial thickening/calcification and signs of ventricular interdependence
questions.explanation: CT and CMR can demonstrate structural pericardial disease and functional consequences.

questions.question: Which issues are relevant to MRI safety? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: All are central to safe MRI practice.

questions.question: In severe aortic stenosis, CT before transcatheter valve implantation is used to assess:
options: Annular dimensions, vascular access and aortic root anatomy
questions.explanation: Pre-TAVI CT provides annular sizing and vascular/aortic root planning.

questions.question: Which MRI finding is typical of intracapsular silicone breast implant rupture?
questions.explanation: The linguine sign represents collapsed implant shell within silicone.

questions.question: In suspected deep neck infection, CT findings favouring an abscess include:
options: A rim-enhancing fluid collection with surrounding inflammatory change
Uniform fat with no inflammatory change
questions.explanation: A rim-enhancing collection with inflammatory change is suspicious for abscess.

questions.question: Which MRI safety issues should be checked before scanning? Choose all that apply.
options: Appropriate screening of equipment entering the room
questions.explanation: MRI safety depends on screening patients, implants and equipment for static-field and RF-related hazards.

questions.question: A large iodinated contrast extravasation with severe pain and neurovascular symptoms requires:
options: Immediate clinical assessment and escalation because compartment syndrome is possible
Further forceful injection through the same IV
questions.explanation: Severe symptoms after extravasation require urgent assessment for tissue injury and compartment syndrome.

questions.question: In a patient with impaired renal function, the decision to use gadolinium-based contrast should consider:
options: Clinical necessity, renal function and the risk profile of the specific agent
The colour of the contrast vial
questions.explanation: Risk assessment depends on indication, kidney function and the selected gadolinium agent.

questions.question: Which statement about radiopharmaceutical safety is correct?
options: Administration should follow justification, optimisation and pregnancy/breastfeeding precautions when relevant
Activity should be maximised regardless of indication
questions.explanation: Nuclear medicine uses ionising radiation and requires appropriate justification, optimisation and patient-specific precautions.

cases.title: Dural-based brain mass
cases.stem: MRI demonstrates a well-defined extra-axial mass with broad dural contact and avid enhancement.

questions.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The morphology is typical of a meningioma.

questions.question: Which finding may be associated with a meningioma?
options: Restricted diffusion in the entire vascular territory
questions.explanation: Adjacent hyperostosis is a recognised associated finding in some meningiomas.

cases.title: Suspicious breast lesion
cases.stem: A 52-year-old woman has a new palpable breast mass. Mammography and ultrasound show an irregular spiculated lesion.

questions.question: How should this lesion be categorised conceptually?
options: Suspicious for malignancy and requiring tissue diagnosis
questions.explanation: An irregular spiculated mass is suspicious and requires diagnostic work-up.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.explanation: Percutaneous biopsy is the standard route to tissue diagnosis for a suspicious breast mass.

cases.title: Screening mammography recall
cases.stem: Screening mammography demonstrates a new cluster of fine pleomorphic calcifications.

questions.question: How should this finding be regarded?
options: A technical artefact in every case
questions.explanation: New grouped fine pleomorphic calcifications are suspicious.

questions.question: A likely next step is:
options: Magnification views and tissue diagnosis according to the completed assessment
questions.explanation: Diagnostic mammographic assessment and biopsy are commonly required for suspicious calcifications.

cases.title: Painful swollen orbit
cases.stem: A febrile patient has painful proptosis and impaired eye movements. Contrast-enhanced CT of the orbits is performed.

questions.question: Which diagnosis is most concerning?
options: Post-septal orbital cellulitis with possible abscess
questions.explanation: Post-septal inflammation/collection is an emergency because of visual and intracranial complications.

questions.question: Which complication should be actively assessed?
questions.explanation: Orbital infection may extend to subperiosteal spaces, cavernous sinus or intracranially.

cases.title: Palpable breast mass with suspicious node
cases.stem: A 52-year-old woman has an irregular breast mass with posterior acoustic shadowing and a morphologically suspicious axillary node.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate next management recommendation?
options: Image-guided biopsy of the breast lesion and assessment/biopsy of the node as appropriate
questions.explanation: Suspicious breast and nodal findings require timely tissue diagnosis and staging assessment.

questions.question: Which information should be included in the report?
options: Lesion size, location, morphology and level of suspicion
questions.explanation: Structured description supports multidisciplinary management.

questions.question: Which response would be potentially unsafe?
options: Calling the lesion clearly benign without justification and ignoring the suspicious node
questions.explanation: False reassurance may delay diagnosis of breast cancer.

cases.title: Neck pain and partial Horner syndrome
cases.stem: A 45-year-old patient develops sudden unilateral neck pain and partial Horner syndrome. CTA of the neck is performed.

questions.question: Which diagnosis should be actively sought?
questions.explanation: Neck pain with partial Horner syndrome is a classic presentation of carotid dissection.

questions.question: Which finding supports the diagnosis?
options: Crescentic mural haematoma and tapered luminal narrowing
questions.explanation: Mural haematoma and tapered stenosis are characteristic imaging features.

questions.question: Which report would be potentially unsafe?
options: Reporting the study as normal despite clear carotid dissection
questions.explanation: Missing a carotid dissection can delay treatment and stroke prevention.
